intro: Two kinds of football grew up in the 1800s. One grew on American college lawns and became the game played on a gridiron. The other was written down in a London tavern in 1863 and became soccer, played on a pitch. Both started with older town games that had crowds, a ball and no written rules.

In this unit you will meet the students, lawyers, teachers and presidents who wrote the rules down. You will see how meetings in Springfield, London, Chicago and Paris turned local games into shared codes. You will also see who was shut out, such as women's teams banned in England in 1921, and when doors opened.

By the end, you can name the bodies that keep each game's rules, like the NCAA, IFAB, FIFA and the IHSA. You can put key dates in order. You can explain why a school field and a World Cup stadium follow the same written rules.
bigQuestion: How did two games with old roots get written rule books, governing bodies and fields that schools and nations could share?

timeline.t: Lord Mayor of London bans football in the city for King Edward II
Cambridge University students write the Cambridge Rules
The Football Association is founded in London and writes 13 laws
Rutgers and Princeton play the first college football game
Colleges form the Intercollegiate Football Association in Springfield, Massachusetts
Four British associations form IFAB to keep the Laws of the Game
FIFA is founded in Paris by seven European associations
A new college body forms and the forward pass becomes legal
Uruguay hosts and wins the first World Cup
Title IX becomes law; IHSA holds its first boys soccer state series
IHSA holds its first state football playoffs
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts the opening game of the World Cup

test.q: What did folk football and cuju have in common?
choices: both were old ball games played before modern rule books
test.why: Folk football in England and cuju in China were both played long before the 1863 laws.

test.q: Where was the first college football game played in 1869?
test.why: Rutgers and Princeton played at New Brunswick on November 6, 1869.

test.q: Which university's visit in 1874 pushed Harvard toward a rugby style?
test.why: McGill University of Montreal played Harvard in 1874 with rugby-style rules.

test.q: Who led the 1880 and 1882 rule changes that created the line of scrimmage and downs?
test.why: Walter Camp of Yale led those rule changes.

test.q: Who was the first Black player named to college football's All-America team?
test.why: William Henry Lewis was named All-America in 1892.

test.q: Why did President Theodore Roosevelt call football men to the White House in 1905?
choices: to ask them to make the game safer
test.why: After many injuries and deaths, Roosevelt asked colleges to make football safer.

test.q: In what year did the college rule body take the name NCAA?
test.why: The IAAUS, formed in 1906, was renamed the NCAA in 1910.

test.q: Which group met in Chicago in 1895 and became the Big Ten?
test.why: Seven university presidents met at the Palmer House and formed the Western Conference.

test.q: Why does Memorial Stadium in Champaign have names on its columns?
choices: they are the names of coaches
they honor Illinois people who died in World War I
they list the first IHSA champions
test.why: The stadium is a memorial to Illinois students and graduates who died in the war.

test.q: What did the Football Association's 1863 laws not allow?
choices: carrying the ball in the hands
test.why: The FA's laws said players could not carry the ball, which split soccer from rugby.

test.q: Which body decides changes to the Laws of the Game?
test.why: IFAB has kept the Laws of the Game since 1886.

test.q: How did soccer rules reach Argentina and Brazil?
choices: teachers, workers and returning students carried them
test.why: People like Alexander Watson Hutton and Charles Miller brought the game and its rules.

test.q: Which statement about the 1930 World Cup is true?
test.why: Uruguay hosted the first World Cup and beat Argentina 4 to 2.

test.q: What happened to women's teams in England between 1921 and 1971?
choices: they wrote the Laws of the Game
the FA banned them from its members' grounds
test.why: The FA's 1921 ban kept women's teams off members' grounds until 1971.

choices: the opening of the 1994 World Cup
test.why: Boys soccer came in 1972, football playoffs in 1974 and girls soccer in 1988.

write.prompt: Who has more power over a game: the people who play it or the bodies that write its rules? Use two or three dated events from this unit, such as the 1863 FA laws, the 1906 football reforms or the FA's 1921 ban, to support your answer.
tips: Name each event with its date, place and the body that acted.
Say who made each rule and who had to follow it.
Compare the gridiron and the pitch rather than calling one better.
Use unit words like convention, reform, federation and ban.
